title: Unify response serializer and gated cache cohesion for GraphQL/REST hot paths
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: The console backend exposes a mix of GraphQL resolvers and REST aggregation endpoints that independently serialize response shapes and apply short-lived in-memory caches. Over time divergent serializers and cache invalidation semantics have caused tail-latency variance, stale UI cards, and duplicated work in downstream metric collection. Goal: introduce a single response-serializer library used by GraphQL resolvers and REST handlers, and replace ad-hoc per-handler caches with a gated cohesion layer that coordinates with the existing KV caching layer. Scope: audit top 15 resolver/REST handlers by qps and payload size; refactor serializer; add feature-flag gated cache adapter; add metrics and canary rollout plan. Out-of-scope: full downstream UI contract changes, major schema reshapes (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: Unified serializer library implemented and published as an internal package and used by top 10 hot handlers behind a feature flag
Gated cache adapter added that delegates to existing KV cache for long-lived keys and in-memory coherence for request-local aggregation
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for targeted endpoints reduced by >=15% in perf harness compared to baseline
No functional regressions in GraphQL contract (integration tests pass) and no increased error rates during canary rollout
Dashboards added: serializer latency breakdown, cache hit/miss by key type, and end-to-end request variance; runbook updated
tasks: Inventory response shapes and serializers for top 15 console handlers
Design unified serializer API and migration compatibility layer
Implement gated cache adapter with TTL semantics compatible with KV-coherence
Add feature flag and internal config toggle for gradual rollout
Instrument detailed metrics and add Grafana panels
Create perf harness scenarios (synthetic + recorded traffic) and run comparisons
Prepare canary plan and rollback steps; coordinate with SRE
Update internal docs and add example usage to SDKs
comments: 2025-11-03 Priya Patel: Kickoff - scoped top 15 handlers by qps using last 30d tracing. Initial audit attached in artifacts. Marcus to take lead on serializer design.

2025-11-04 Marcus Lee: Drafted serializer API (v1): normalize field ordering, stable deterministic marshalling for nested lists, and contextual hooks for redaction. Pushed draft in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8392 (WIP).

2025-11-05 Elena Garcia (SRE): Suggested we avoid global in-memory caches on hosts with bursty traffic; recommended gated adapter that can fall back to per-request aggregation during bursts. Marking as dependency for autoscaling tests.

2025-11-05 Marcus Lee: Implemented gated cache adapter prototype. Local perf shows 18% 95th reduction for /api/overview in synthetic harness. Will add integration tests and metrics before feature flag flip.
2025-11-06 Priya Patel: PM review - prioritize endpoints that cause UI jitter (routes list, token billing summary). Approved estimate but please add canary checklist and alert thresholds.
2025-11-06 Marcus Lee: Added canary checklist in artifacts and created Grafana dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console/serializer-cohesion
notes: Trade-offs discussed: deterministic serialization ordering simplifies caching and reduces diff noise but may hide intentional non-determinism in telemetry payloads; opted to keep an opt-in hook for telemetry. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and invalidate gated cache namespace, monitored by SRE; expected blast radius minimal because change is behind flag. Next steps after canary: extend to remaining handlers and consider publishing serializer to internal registry for non-console services.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Audit + design (2d). Phase 2: Implement serializer + gated adapter behind feature flag + unit tests (3d). Phase 3: Perf/integration tests + dashboards (1d). Phase 4: Canary rollout and monitoring (2d).
estimated_risks: Cache coherence edge cases causing stale UI tiles
Serializer change causing nondeterministic order in third-party consumption
Increased memory pressure from in-memory gating during burst traffic
